question: Pandit Ram Narayan was a popular __________ player who is credited with making the instrument as a solo concert instrument.
solution:
The correct answer is** __Sarangi__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​**

__
 
• The sarangi is a bowed instrument that was made popular by Indian artist** Pandit Ram Narayan **as a solo performance instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
• He also became the** first sarangi performer to achieve fame on a global scale.**
 
• The **sarangi is played with a bow just like a violin**, but in contrast to the violin, it is held vertically with the sound chamber below.
 
• It normally has **three primary strings**, with a fourth string serving as a drone occasionally.
 
• A** solo concerto** is a type of music in which an orchestra plays behind a single solo instrument that plays the melodic line.
 
• A **solo concerto has three movements:** a quick section, a slow section, and then another fast section.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__​

 
• Mridangam:

 
 
• The two-headed drum known as the** mridangam, it is used in southern Indian Karnatak music.**
 
• It has an outline resembling an extended hexagon and is made of wood in the form of an angular barrel. India's top-ranked mridangam player is** Karaikudi R Mani**.
 
• Mani, who received instruction from renowned tutors, has developed a distinctive playing style characterised by high virtuosity and enticing **sound quality.**
 
 
 
• **Ghatam**:
 
 
• **Ghatam, a huge, conical clay water pot** used in India as a percussion instrument.
 
• The ghatam lacks a membrane covering its mouth, unlike other Indian percussion instruments like the** tabla and mridangam**. **Ujjwal Kumar, a ghatam player,** has lofty goals for the common 'desi' musical instrument.
 
 
 
• **Alghoza**
 
 
• A bamboo-made stringed instrument is called an** ****Alghoza.**
 
• It is a significant **Rajasthani folk instrument. **
 
• A double-flute frequently played by the Alwar-based Meo community.
